claims.question: Do the frozen LAM-JEPA planner/target components improve ARC validation performance over matched supervised and ablated controls?
claims.hypothesis: The full frozen LAM-JEPA system will outperform the matched supervised control and show positive planner and target contributions under the preregistered validation protocol.
claims.mechanism: Latent-action/JEPA system with planner and target components whose causal contribution is probed through frozen no-planner and no-target ablations. No stronger mechanism statement is inferred here.

novelty_boundary.established_technique: JEPA-style latent prediction, supervised controls, component ablation
novelty_boundary.combination_novelty: possible, not independently audited in this recovery
novelty_boundary.mechanism_novelty: not supported by current ARC evidence
novelty_boundary.empirical_novelty: reproducible negative/inconclusive result under the frozen ARC protocol

claims.primary_claim: The frozen ARC validation protocol reproducibly does not support superiority, planner benefit, or target benefit.
claims.falsifier: Matched supervised and/or ablated controls match or exceed the full system, or paired component effects fail to show the preregistered positive mechanism contribution.
claims.next_gate: Paper conversion, provenance chain, related-work originality audit, external/independent review. No ARC rescue experiment.

claims.question: Can the current adaptive robust mechanism beat strong fixed robust controls across adverse noise while adapting faster to persistent shifts without losing clean behavior?
claims.hypothesis: The frozen PABIM candidate will pass clean non-inferiority and robustness guardrails and satisfy the persistent-shift advancement gate against strong fixed robust controls.
claims.mechanism: Adaptive robust estimator/memory candidate intended to distinguish observation corruption from legitimate regime change; this ledger does not infer mechanism detail beyond the frozen implementation and measured adaptation/robustness behavior.

novelty_boundary.established_technique: Huber/clipped/Student-t robust estimation, changepoint/switching baselines, recurrent comparators
novelty_boundary.implementation_novelty: project-specific PABIM harness and adaptation rule
novelty_boundary.mechanism_novelty: not established because the current candidate fails strong-control and persistent-shift gates

claims.primary_claim: The current PABIM candidate fails the frozen strong-robust-control and persistent-shift development gates and is not authorized for confirmatory seeds.
claims.falsifier: Failure of any frozen advancement guardrail, especially strong fixed-control or persistent-shift performance.
claims.next_gate: Negative-result conversion. Any successor must document changed hypothesis, motivation, falsifier and frozen protocol before new confirmatory evaluation.

claims.question: Does the non-Gaussian learned memory arm outperform matched standard and Gaussian/reference memory under adverse conditions at equal capacity and runtime memory?
claims.hypothesis: B3 will improve >=5% over B2 and >=3% over B1 on the frozen adverse aggregate while keeping clean regression <=2%.
claims.mechanism: Learned memory variants B0/B1/B2/B3 designed to isolate the incremental contribution of the proposed non-Gaussian memory under equal parameter and memory budgets.

novelty_boundary.established_technique: Transformer/recurrent memory comparisons, robust statistical readouts/reference assumptions

claims.primary_claim: NGMT v0.1 reproducibly misses both frozen adverse-condition superiority gates while passing the clean-regression guardrail.
claims.falsifier: B3 fails either adverse improvement gate or violates clean regression.
claims.next_gate: Negative-result package. No v0.1 retuning; redesign only as a separately versioned successor.

claims.question: Does the eigen/spectral latent formulation improve the frozen primary covariance-matrix forecasting target over strong classical spectral and simple linear baselines?
claims.hypothesis: Eigen-JEPA will beat the strongest frozen classical/raw/log/PCA baseline on covariance-matrix MSE.
claims.mechanism: Eigen/spectral representation of covariance dynamics compared against raw, log, PCA and persisted-eigenspace spectral ridge controls.

novelty_boundary.established_technique: spectral decomposition, ridge regression, PCA, covariance forecasting
novelty_boundary.mechanism_novelty: not supported on current primary metric
novelty_boundary.empirical_novelty: strong classical baselines dominate or match the current method

claims.primary_claim: The current method is baseline-dominated/non-superior on the frozen primary covariance-matrix MSE.
claims.falsifier: Any competent frozen baseline matches or improves primary covariance-matrix MSE.
dangerous_baselines: spectral eigenvalue ridge with persisted eigenspace
claims.next_gate: Reconcile row-count provenance, then negative-result conversion. Multi-dataset work is a new frozen generalization question, not a metric rescue.

claims.question: Does a typed/validated structured intermediate representation improve executable CAD generation over a matched direct-generation approach?
claims.hypothesis: Structured IR will improve syntax/execution/geometry/constraint success over direct generation under matched provider, model, information, token and retry budgets.
claims.mechanism: Natural-language input is converted through a typed/validated IR before CAD execution, intended to reduce syntax/constraint failures relative to unconstrained direct generation.

novelty_boundary.established_technique: structured intermediate representations, constrained generation, program synthesis, retrieval/search baselines
novelty_boundary.mechanism_novelty: not yet isolated against matched learned direct/constrained/retrieval baselines
novelty_boundary.empirical_novelty: controlled held-out-template advantage in the frozen v1 screen

claims.primary_claim: On the frozen controlled v1 benchmark the structured pipeline scores 19/20 versus 12/20 for the direct baseline and yields non-empty STL for 12/12 valid cases.
claims.falsifier: A matched direct/constrained/retrieval baseline closes the execution/geometry/constraint-success gap, or the advantage disappears on broader OOD cases.
claims.next_gate: Freeze and run one same-provider learned direct-vs-IR benchmark with broader OOD, ambiguous, constraint-heavy and impossible requests.

claims.question: Is APEN's rare-event benefit specifically caused by correctly aligned temporal salience rather than generic memory capacity or arbitrary salience values?
claims.hypothesis: Correct salience alignment will outperform uniform memory, while shuffled or distribution-matched random salience will erase most of the rare-event gain.
claims.mechanism: Salience-weighted memory prioritizes temporally aligned rare-event information; the specificity test randomizes alignment while preserving comparable salience distributions.

novelty_boundary.established_technique: attention/memory weighting, salience heuristics, recurrent/attention memory controls
novelty_boundary.mechanism_novelty: bounded synthetic evidence supports alignment specificity
novelty_boundary.empirical_novelty: prospective synthetic mechanism ablation with exact replay

claims.primary_claim: Correct temporal salience alignment matters in the existing synthetic ridge-readout task; shuffled/randomized salience erases the measured rare-event gain.
claims.falsifier: A same-information learned memory control matches the gain, or salience randomization preserves the effect under the frozen test.
claims.next_gate: Matched learned recurrent/attention control plus preregistered naturalistic salience-quality stress.

claims.question: Can the audit reliably detect injected coordinate leakage, and does the same methodology reveal meaningful blind spots in real multilingual encoders after strong nuisance controls?
claims.hypothesis: The synthetic injected-coordinate audit will pass its frozen verifier, and a separately frozen real-encoder extension will show effects that survive centering/random-group/random-subspace controls.
claims.mechanism: Probe/audit design tests whether representation structure exposes injected epistemic coordinates; real-encoder claims are explicitly separate from the synthetic diagnostic.

novelty_boundary.established_technique: representation probing, synthetic leakage diagnostics, nuisance/randomized controls
novelty_boundary.mechanism_novelty: not established for real multilingual encoders

claims.primary_claim: The synthetic audit reproduces within its frozen boundary and has an independent verifier.
claims.falsifier: A real-encoder effect disappears under preregistered centering/random-group/random-subspace controls or fails independent reproduction.
claims.next_gate: Freeze real-encoder datasets, probes, controls, primary statistic, seeds and falsifier before execution.
